clue.text: Reading is a novel experience for three funny boatmen

definitions.text: Reading is a novel experience for three funny boatmen

parts.words: Reading is a novel experience for three funny boatmen
parts.note: Reading is the Berkshire town on the river through London, and Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat sends its three boatmen along that river past it

explanation.surface: A book group finds reading a comic novel about three boatmen a fresh experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the activity of reading a book; it is the town of Reading, which stands on the river where the novel's comic boating trip takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the town and the voyage of Jerome's three men are located on London's great river.

clue.text: Staffs versifier can't decide it seems

explanation.surface: A poet from Staffordshire seems unable to make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes, author of The Highwayman, was born in Wolverhampton, then in Staffordshire (Staffs). Someone who says 'no, yes' cannot decide.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Alfred Noyes came from Staffordshire, and saying no then yes is the speech of a ditherer.

clue.text: She treats as guests a great many English saints

parts.note: a host is a great many, as in a host of problems
SS is the abbreviation for saints, the plural of St

explanation.surface: A woman entertains a crowd of English saints as her guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and entertains visitors is their hostess.

clue.text: Du Maurier's novel hat

explanation.surface: A novel by du Maurier about headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: George du Maurier's 1894 novel Trilby gave its name to the soft felt hat worn in its stage version.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is the title of George du Maurier's novel, and also a soft felt brimmed hat named after it.

clue.text: No wings wildly circle pasture treated thus

indicators.note: wildly says the letters that follow are thrown into a disordered new arrangement

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A wingless creature runs wildly in circles round a field that has been treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' shuffles O (a circle) with PASTURE; 'treated thus' only links the wordplay to the definition, saying the letters are handled this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Apterous is the zoologist's term for insects lacking flight organs, from Greek for wingless.

clue.text: Dressed up for the ceremony with a gown in the end

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other, here the garment within the final word

parts.note: the end is simply END
a gown is a robe

explanation.surface: Someone finally put on a gown to dress up for a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enrobed is to be clad in formal robes, as for an official occasion.

clue.text: It's unpalatable to have to take it down

definitions.text: to have to take it down

explanation.surface: Something nasty-tasting that must still be swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both unpleasant to accept and, literally, difficult to get down the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpalatable idea is one people struggle to accept, and something literally difficult to gulp down fits the phrase too.

clue.text: See 23
How the tall-story-teller lies and lies

definitions.text: How the tall-story-teller lies and lies

parts.words: How the tall-story-teller lies and lies
parts.note: the teller of tall stories is read as a tall person stretched out when lying down, and also as someone telling long, drawn-out untruths

explanation.surface: A teller of tall stories keeps on lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies' is used twice in two senses: reclining, which a tall person does over a long stretch, and telling untruths, which a yarn-spinner does lengthily.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for a long time or in great detail, and also stretched out over a big distance.

clue.text: Put alongside in a ship where the depth 1is immeasurable

indicators.note: in says the word for alongside goes inside the vessel phrase

parts.note: SS is steamship, the prefix of a ship's name
by means next to, alongside

explanation.surface: Moored beside a ship over water too deep to measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm or bottomless pit is a place whose deepness cannot be sounded.

clue.text: Explain what foreigners mean to the natives?

definitions.text: Explain what foreigners mean to the natives?

parts.words: Explain what foreigners mean to the natives?
parts.note: putting a visitor's words into the local language for the people who live there is the work of a translator

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to translate for visitors abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To render foreign speech in the listeners' own tongue is to translate, or explain its meaning.

clue.text: Apparently one of Hell's Angels: take his arms away?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so Hell itself, and his angels are its company
one of a group is a member of it

explanation.surface: A biker gang member is threatened with having his arms cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' tells you to read the answer as two words: DIS (Hell) and MEMBER, a member of Hell's band. Taking off arms is dismembering, with arms as limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut off the limbs of a body.

clue.text: Thorny subject among puffers

explanation.surface: A prickly topic for smokers.
explanation.walkthrough: A briar is a thorny bush, and also a tobacco pipe made from briar root, a talking point among pipe smokers (puffers).
explanation.definitionFit: Briar is a prickly shrub, and its root wood makes the favourite pipe of smokers.

clue.text: Slice of loaf is hard, but doesn't excuse such conduct

definitions.note: the clue names behaviour, a noun; the answer is the adjective describing such behaviour

indicators.note: a slice is a portion cut out, so the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: Stale bread is no excuse for boorish behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Loutish, clumsy behaviour is described as that of an oaf.

clue.text: Obese guide outworn

parts.note: obese means fat

indicators.note: out says the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An overweight guide is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'outworn' is two words, 'out' (the anagram signal for GUIDE, giving IGUED) and 'worn', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn here means tired out, exhausted.

clue.text: Four-horse chariot placed before Latvian city square

indicators.note: placed before tells the solver to set the square ahead of the city in the answer

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A chariot drawn by four horses is set up in a square in Riga.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadriga is the Roman chariot pulled by a team of four horses abreast.

clue.text: Organise a relay or take part in it?

explanation.surface: Running a relay: organising it or competing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: To run a race can mean to stage it as an organiser or to compete in it as a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both staging a race and competing in it are described by the phrase.

clue.text: Take care! Hunter isn't accurate

explanation.surface: A warning that a hunter is a poor shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover; one that is out keeps the wrong time.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch out is a shouted warning to be careful, and a timepiece that is out is inaccurate.

clue.text: Chickened out?

parts.note: read literally, chicks came out of their eggs, rather than someone losing their nerve

explanation.surface: Someone lost their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that have produced their chicks have done so by cracking open.

clue.text: A spare word?

parts.note: a word meaning sparing or economical, rather than an unused extra word

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean thrifty and meagre, which is what a thrifty person is.

clue.text: UN adore prepared words repeatedly and poetically expressed

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The UN prepares a statement full of poetic repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain repeated from its opening line.

clue.text: Cherry's concoction could make Royal Highness sick

indicators.note: could make suggests these letters can be reworked into something new

parts.note: RH is the abbreviation for Royal Highness

explanation.surface: A cherry drink could make a royal feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear brandy distilled from cherries.

clue.text: Little exercise for the locoman to do in the evening

definitions.text: for the locoman to do in the evening

explanation.surface: A train driver takes a bit of exercise at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Light training is gentle exercise; a locoman (engine driver) driving at night would be lighting his train.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle workout is light physical training, and an engine driver at dusk would switch on his train's lamps.

clue.text: Cornelian in tears — and so was Ruth here

indicators.note: in tears says the word is ripped up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Ruth wept over a cornelian stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale pictures Ruth, the Biblical widow, standing 'in tears amid the alien corn', so 'in tears' also serves her picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats placed the Biblical Ruth, homesick, among foreign fields of grain.

clue.text: Oh, Ma! Hear Tyrone's settlement

indicators.note: Hear says the answer is a word that sounds like the words before it when spoken

parts.note: an exclamation to a mother, said as two syllables

explanation.surface: A child calls out to their mother about a town in Tyrone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone is a county of Northern Ireland, and Omagh its county town, pronounced like 'Oh, Ma'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Where warning shots may be fired concerning business expenses

definitions.text: Where warning shots may be fired

explanation.surface: Warning shots fired over business costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Warning shots are fired over people's heads; overheads are also a firm's running costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning burst is fired above the crowd, and fixed running costs of a firm are its overheads.

clue.text: Former performance on demand

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: An old stage act performed on request.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, as in exacting payment.

clue.text: I'd get permit, though possibly that's just a vain fancy

parts.note: to permit is to let

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone muses that getting a permit is probably a pipe dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' and 'that's just' are links; the synonym LET (permit) stands between the fodder words, so it joins I'D and THOUGH in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle notion is a daydream with no practical purpose, a mere whim.
